difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma with its two sentences: a morphism of algebraic spaces which is locally of finite presentation is locally of finite type, and a morphism of finite presentation is of finite type (source lines 5744-5748). The proof uses the source-and-target presentation of local finite presentation, reduces to the scheme morphism h, applies the scheme statement that locally of finite presentation implies locally of finite type, and reads the property back for the morphism of algebraic spaces; the second sentence adds quasi-compactness, which is part of finite presentation.
